answer: Reef-and-Prism Keying: each identity gets a unique agent key, and every action must carry a fresh proof derived from a secret split across a quorum of independent registrars that bridge separate networks. Registrars cross-check key derivations against distinct hardware roots, so cloning forces the attacker to acquire and maintain all quorum shares per clone. Marginal clones therefore cost full quorum share refresh fees plus repeated hardware attestation, making each extra identity strictly negative-EV.
